analysis.investment_thesis: Excelsoft is a niche EdTech SaaS play in assessment and proctoring — a space with genuine post-COVID tailwinds — growing revenue at a respectable 17.7% CAGR, but EBITDA is contracting and the 2025 earnings spike is inflated by non-recurring "Other Income" of ₹15 Cr, making the cheap-looking forward P/E of 13x misleading. Wait for cleaner profit quality before committing capital.
key_strengths: Aggressive debt paydown: borrowings slashed from ₹168 Cr to ₹45 Cr over 5 years, D/E now just 0.12 — financial leverage risk is disappearing fast
Consistent OCF: positive all 5 years (₹53–63 Cr range) showing real cash generation, not accounting fiction
Niche EdTech SaaS with global reach (North America, Europe, APAC) in a structurally growing market for online proctoring and assessments
key_risks: EBITDA trend is contracting (8.1% CAGR vs 17.7% revenue growth) — costs are growing faster than revenue, killing operating leverage
2025 net profit of ₹35 Cr includes ₹15 Cr 'Other Income' (vs ₹2 Cr prior year) — strip that out and core operating profit improvement is much more modest
ROE of 10.4% is below my 12% floor — returns on capital are unimpressive for a SaaS company that should have asset-light economics
red_flags: Other Income spike (₹2→₹15 Cr) artificially flatters 2025 EPS and the forward P/E of 13x — forward estimates may assume a non-recurring gain recurs
Trailing PEG of ~1.56 (P/E 27.6 / 17.7% revenue growth) breaches my 1.5 threshold — not cheap enough for the growth on offer
Very low institutional interest: FII 1.37%, DII 4.06% — smart money hasn't validated the story yet
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Peter Lynch here. I love the story on the surface — small Mysore-based SaaS firm selling online proctoring (EasyProctor) and assessments (SARAS) to global universities. This is a business I could understand from observing the post-COVID shift to remote exams. Revenue has grown from ₹103 Cr to ₹233 Cr over five years (17.7% CAGR), and the balance sheet transformation is genuinely impressive — they've cut borrowings by ₹123 Cr while equity doubled to ₹388 Cr. OCF has been consistently positive every single year. This has the bones of a good niche compounder.

But the numbers underneath tell a messier story. EBITDA has barely moved — ₹59 Cr in 2020, ₹87 Cr in 2025, a meager 8.1% CAGR — meaning revenue growth isn't flowing through to profits. The 2025 net profit jump to ₹35 Cr looks exciting until you see ₹15 Cr came from "Other Income," likely asset sales or non-recurring items. Normalize that, and core earnings are probably ₹20 Cr — closer to the ₹13 Cr earned in 2024 than the headline suggests. ROE sits at a disappointing 10.4%, well below what I'd expect from a SaaS business with 48% gross margins. At a trailing PEG of ~1.56, I'm not getting paid enough for the growth risk. Watch for two consecutive quarters of clean margin expansion before getting excited.
